newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha barely moved, near-term spreads even.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha barely moved, near-term spreads even.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices moved sideways in lacklustre afternoon trade on Wednesday, with traders watching the progress of talks on Iraqi crude oil exports carefully, market participants said.
"Traders appear to be reluctant to take up firm positions as they aren't sure how the possible resumption of Iraqi crude oil exports will affect the market," one naphtha dealer said.
Bids for second-half September open-spec naphtha were notionally assessed at $207.00 per tonne, against offers at $208.00. It changed hands several times at $207.00 in late trading on Tuesday.
In spreads, second-half September/second-half October was indicated at minus 25 cents/plus 50 cents.
In low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) trading, persistently high spot prices were forcing buying interest in Japan to shift to low sulphur crude oil, traders said.

Even though low sulphur crude oil prices are still higher than LSWR on a free on board basis, it is currently more economical for power firms to burn low sulphur crude oil for power generation as tariffs on crude oil are lower than those on LSWR, they said.
